rows.name: Indus Valley Civilization

Name each feature.

Build a brick street with blocks.
Ask each child to name one feature.

rows.name: Vowel team words: ow, oi, ear, air, ure
steps: Write words on cards (cow, coin, ear, hair, cure) and set out five headings: ow, oi, ear, air, ure.
Ask pairs to take turns drawing a card, reading it aloud and placing it under its heading.
Call out a pattern and have children hold up a matching card.
Read each column aloud together.
Finish with a quick race to find one card for each heading.

levels.3: Unseen words like owl, point, chair and pure are read aloud and then used in a spoken sentence.

rows.name: Ins and outs: ports and peripherals
steps: Set out a computer, mouse, keyboard, speaker and a printer for children to look at.
Name each part aloud and let children touch it.
Point to the sockets on the computer and say these are ports.
Sort the parts into a ports group and a peripherals group on a mat.
Ask each child to point to one port and one peripheral and say its name.

levels.3: For a new job such as printing or listening, the right peripheral is picked and named.

rows.name: Sharing and grouping: division with arrays
steps: Give each pair 12 counters and 3 paper plates.
Ask them to deal the counters one at a time so every plate gets the same.
Count the counters on one plate and say the number.
Line the counters up in 3 rows to make an array and say the division sentence.
Read a sharing word problem, such as 12 sweets for 4 friends, and solve it with counters.

levels.3: A sharing story with new numbers is solved with counters and an array, and the answer is said with its unit.

rows.name: Filling and measuring containers

Fill two containers and say which is fuller, which is empty, which holds more.

Show a measuring jug and point to the 1 litre line.
Fill the jug to a line chosen by the educator and read the scale aloud.

levels.3: A guess is made first, then a jug is poured and read in litres or millilitres, and the guess is checked.

rows.name: Hot, warm, cool and cold: reading a thermometer
steps: Set out cups of safe hot, warm, cool and cold water and ice.
Ask children to feel each cup or card and sort things as hot, warm, cool or cold.
Show a large classroom thermometer and point to the scale.
Place it in two cups in turn and read the number with the educator.
Write each reading with the unit degrees Celsius on a recording sheet.

rows.name: Chance experiments: rolling a cube and picking from a bag
steps: Give each pair a number cube and a bag of red and blue cubes.
Say which things will always, sometimes or never happen with the cube.
Roll the cube ten times and make a tally mark for each number.
Pick a cube from the bag ten times, put it back and tally the colours.
Say which outcome came up most and whether that was likely.
rows.note: Steps built from the unit's syllabus bullets; no plan cell names a runnable activity. Educator should confirm.

levels.0: The recording sheet has no tally marks, since nothing was rolled or picked.
levels.1: Ten rolls are made but only a few tally marks are recorded, or the tallies have no total.
levels.2: A tally of ten rolls or ten picks fills the sheet, and the outcome with most marks is said.
levels.3: A prediction about a bag with new colours is made first, then the tally is compared with it.

rows.name: Symmetry in shapes and patterns
steps: Fold paper shapes in half and see if the sides match.
Draw the fold line on each symmetric shape.
Give pairs half a drawing and ask them to complete the mirror image.
Sort shape cards into symmetric and not symmetric.
Look for symmetry in a leaf, a butterfly and a building picture.

levels.0: No line is drawn on any shape and none is pointed to.
levels.1: A line is drawn on a shape, but the two sides it makes do not match.
levels.2: A fold line splits a drawn shape into two matching halves and is pointed to.
levels.3: A leaf or building picture is checked for symmetry, and the line is drawn or its absence is said.

rows.name: Left, right, directions and turns
steps: Say left and right while raising the matching hand.
Play Simon says using left, right, forward and back.
Practise quarter, half and full turns on the spot.
Turn clockwise, then counter-clockwise, in a circle.
Ask a partner to follow two directions you give.
rows.note: Steps built from the unit's syllabus bullets; no plan cell names a runnable activity. Educator should confirm.

levels.0: No object is pointed to when the educator asks which is on the left or right.

levels.2: Objects on the left and on the right are pointed to correctly when asked.
levels.3: Two directions with a quarter turn are given to a partner who follows them to a spot.

rows.name: Grids and routes

Place a toy in a square and ask for its row and column.
Give each pair a paper grid with pictures in some squares.
Ask them to say where a picture is using row and column.
Draw and follow a short route across the grid.

levels.3: A route drawn across a new grid is described with rows and columns to a partner.

rows.name: Level 3 revision: long vowels and consonant blends
steps: Spread word cards with long vowel words (cake, boat, tree) and blend words (flag, stop, plum) face down on the mat.
Let children take turns turning over a card and reading it aloud.
Check each read with the pair; a correct read keeps the card.
Ask pairs to sort their kept cards into a long vowel pile and a blend pile.
Count the cards each pair kept and read the piles aloud together.

levels.2: Long vowel words such as cake and boat, and blend words such as flag and plum, are read aloud from the cards.
levels.3: Unseen cards such as stream or frost are read smoothly from a fresh set, with the long vowel or blend pointed out.

rows.name: R-controlled vowel words: ar, or, ur, er
steps: Make cards of ar, or, ur and er words (car, fork, burn, fern) and lay out four hoops labelled ar, or, ur, er.
Ask each child to read a card aloud and place it in the matching hoop.
Have a partner check the choice by reading the hoop's words aloud.
Mix the cards and play again with a new partner.
Finish by reading every hoop's words together.
rows.note: Steps built from the syllabus bullets of this unit; no plan cell names a runnable activity for it. Educator should confirm.

levels.0: Cards remain unread and no word is placed in an ar, or, ur or er hoop.
levels.1: Reading of r-controlled words is slow, with each letter sounded and the ar or or sound named only from a prompt card.
levels.2: Words with ar, or, ur and er, such as car, fork, burn and fern, are read from the cards with the r-controlled sound correct.
levels.3: New words such as shark, storm, church and number are read aloud and the spelling pattern in each is named.

rows.name: Open and closed syllable sorting
steps: Prepare word cards (go, me, he, hot, sit, cup) and draw two columns headed open and closed on the board.
Show one open and one closed example and say the vowel sound in each.
Let children read a card aloud and place it in a column.
Ask them to point to the last letter to justify the choice.
Count the cards in each column together.

levels.2: Open-syllable words such as go and me sit in one column and closed-syllable words such as hot and cup in the other.
levels.3: A two-syllable word like robot or napkin is split, and each part is placed in a column with a reason said aloud.

Show how each pattern sounds and read one word for each.
Ask pairs to take turns reading a card and ticking its pattern on a list.
Play match: find two cards with the same pattern and read them aloud.
Read all the matched pairs together.

rows.name: Blending CCVCC words
steps: Write CCVCC words on cards (stamp, blend, crisp, trunk, plant) and draw five sound boxes on a mat for each pair.
Say the word slowly and have children push a counter into each box for each sound.
Sweep a finger under the letters and blend the sounds into the word.
Ask the partner to read the next card the same way.
Collect the words that were read correctly in a list.
rows.note: Steps built from the syllabus bullets of this unit; no plan cell names a runnable activity for it. Educator should confirm.

levels.0: Five-sound words like stamp and trunk are left unread, with no sounds spoken in order.
levels.1: Beginning blend and ending blend are each said, but the middle vowel is skipped and the word is not joined up.
levels.2: Sounds in a CCVCC word such as stamp are blended left to right into one spoken word.
levels.3: A word not seen in practice, such as clamp or frost, is blended aloud and then written in five sound boxes.
